title: Convex Markov Games: A New Frontier for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

repair_verification.details: Existential stationarity correction verified analytically. No unique stochastic-kernel repair or experimental rerun.

summary: Two local defects: negative transition probabilities in published warehouse specification and incorrect universal selected-supergradient reading of Lemma 3. General equilibrium existence and exploitability bound survive checked arguments.

problems.title: Negative transition probabilities in the published warehouse specification
problems.claim: The listing defines a robot-warehouse transition kernel P:S x A -> Delta(S).
problems.location: Appendix F.2 pp21-24, especially mixed-speed columns at s=0
assumptions: Residual next-state-0 probability assigned as one minus other entries
problems.check: Evaluate three assigned nonzero destination probabilities (4/5,1/5,1/5), then residual 1-6/5=-1/5.
problems.result: Column (-1/5,4/5,1/5,1/5) sums to 1 but is not a probability vector; reversed mixed action similarly invalid.
problems.counterevidence: Source pages visually verified. A different historical implementation could have been used; no provenance establishing identity is available.
problems.impact: Literal published domain cannot be reproduced as a stochastic Markov game. Actual Section5.4 empirical numbers not independently falsified.
problems.remaining_work: Obtain actual historical kernel or author-specified corrected kernel and rerun warehouse results.

acceptance_check.truth_and_assumptions: The warehouse listing explicitly describes transition probabilities; the mixed-action columns contain -1/5.
acceptance_check.decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence: Both columns sum to one, so the printed column-sum assertion cannot detect the violation of nonnegativity. The historical experiment kernel is not established by the listing.
acceptance_check.core_dependency_and_severity: Minor: invalid published domain specification, without refuting the general equilibrium theorem or exploitability upper bound. Historical numerical effects remain Needs Evidence.
acceptance_check.correction_scope: No unique corrected kernel is justified; identifying the actual experimental kernel and re-evaluating its experiment remain unperformed.

problems.title: KKT existence does not imply zero projection for every selected supergradient
problems.claim: Strictly-positive best response iff its projected-gradient norm vanishes, followed by arbitrary generalized-gradient selection.
assumptions: One player, one state, two actions
gamma=0, initial mass1 and valid self-loop dynamics
mu=(1/2,1/2) strictly positive and unique maximizer
g=(-1,0) is a valid utility supergradient
problems.check: A=(1,1); projection I-A^T(AA^T)^-1 A sends g to (-1/2,1/2). Verify supporting inequality u(z)<=-z1 and optimality max(mu1,mu2)>=1/2.
problems.result: Squared projected norm1/2 at best response. KKT only guarantees existence of e.g. g0=(-1/2,-1/2) with zero projection.
problems.counterevidence: Differentiable case is valid; existential reading is valid. The upper-bound theorem remains valid for every admissible finite supergradient.
problems.impact: Local nonsmooth necessity/quantifier defect. No established failure of core exploitability bound or any historical experiment.

correction.statement: At a strictly positive feasible point, under finite-supergradient/KKT conditions, optimality iff there exists a utility supergradient in range(A^T), equivalently with zero tangent projection.
correction.limits: No guarantee for an arbitrary autodiff selection; no convergence theorem added.

acceptance_check.truth_and_assumptions: Lemma 3's necessity argument treats a supporting supergradient selection as arbitrary, although KKT supplies an existential selection.
acceptance_check.decisive_evidence_and_counterevidence: For u=-max on the two-action simplex, mu=(1/2,1/2) is optimal but g=(-1,0) has projected squared norm 1/2. The supporting choice (-1/2,-1/2) has zero projection.
acceptance_check.core_dependency_and_severity: Minor: the selected-supergradient equivalence is false; the core exploitability upper bound survives for each finite supergradient. The independent equilibrium-existence clarification retains joint continuity.
acceptance_check.correction_scope: State existence of a zero-projection supergradient at the positive optimum. No convergence guarantee for a modified algorithm is inferred.

clarifications.summary: The upper-hemicontinuity contractibility inference is insufficient by itself. An independent full-support initial-distribution plus entropy perturbation proof verifies the existence conclusion, so no false-theorem finding is made.
